summary: recordings export's local-first-then-cloud-fallback is a documented contract (README.md), not optional behavior: a local SQLite miss must attempt GET /meetings/{meetingId}/recordings (treating the query as a literal meeting ID/UUID) and download recording_files[].download_url with the CLI's own auth header before erroring. A regen that drops the cloud attempt silently breaks that documented contract for every cloud-only meeting.
reason: newRecordingsExportCmd immediately returned "no local recording matching %q" on a local_recordings SQLite miss, with no cloud attempt, despite README.md explicitly documenting "Resolve a recording ID against local first, fall back to cloud (downloading if needed)". The reusable building block already existed: GET /meetings/{meetingId}/recordings is generated as `meetings recordings get` and returns recording_files with download_url per file. Zoom's recording download_url values are not pre-signed public URLs -- they require the same S2S bearer credential as the API call itself, so the fallback reuses client.Client's own Config.AuthHeader()/HTTPClient rather than an unauthenticated fetch.
validated_outcome: go build/go vet clean. Investigated the finding's "likely" hedge on `recordings recent --source cloud` separately: that command reads a local cloud_recordings SQLite table populated only by a separate `recordings cloud list` sync step and its own source comment says "Honest empty list otherwise" -- by-design local caching, not a documented live-fallback claim, so it was left unchanged.
